data.name: BL21(DE3) Chemical Transformation with pET28a
data.purpose: Introduce a plasmid into BL21(DE3) competent E. coli cells for protein expression.
materials: LB agar plate with appropriate antibiotic
42 C heat block or water bath

steps.text: Thaw 1 tube of BL21(DE3) competent cells on ice.
Add 200ng of {{ph:1774125436234-cac9aa958fe75}} DNA to the cells and gently flick to mix.
Incubate the mixture on ice for 30 min.
Heat shock the cells at 42 C for 45 s, then immediately place them back on ice for 1 min.
Add 1 mL of SOC medium and recover the cells at 37 C with shaking for 1 h.
Plate 100 uL of the recovery culture onto an LB agar plate containing Kanamycin.
Incubate the plate at 37 C for overnight until colonies appear.

data.troubleshooting:
Problem: No colonies on plate; Possible cause: Competent cells lost efficiency or antibiotic selection was incorrect; Solution: Use fresh competent cells and verify the plasmid resistance marker matches the plate antibiotic
Problem: Too many background colonies; Possible cause: Contamination or insufficient antibiotic concentration; Solution: Prepare fresh selective plates and use sterile technique throughout

data.name: Small-Scale Overnight Starter Culture
data.purpose: Prepare a starter culture from a single bacterial colony for downstream expression or plasmid preparation.
materials: Sterile culture tube or baffled flask

steps.text: Add {{ph:1774024647315-9f03b8d734f3c}} of LB medium containing {{ph:1774024647315-9ce336955a66c}} antibiotic to a sterile culture tube.
Pick a single colony from a fresh plate and inoculate the medium.
Incubate the culture at 37 C with shaking at {{ph:1774024647315-09eb7ed8adca9}} for {{ph:1774024647315-82400c92a18e08}}.
Inspect the culture for turbidity and record the culture ID, date, and plasmid name in the notebook.

data.troubleshooting:
Problem: Culture does not grow; Possible cause: Colony was not viable or antibiotic concentration was too high; Solution: Restart from a fresh colony and confirm the correct antibiotic and concentration were used
Problem: Culture appears contaminated; Possible cause: Non-sterile handling during inoculation; Solution: Discard the culture and repeat using stricter sterile technique

protocol:1774024680081-6b02b28fd6d39.label: IPTG-Induced Recombinant Protein Expression in BL21(DE3)

data.purpose: Express a recombinant protein in BL21(DE3) cells using IPTG induction.

steps.text: Inoculate {{ph:1774024680081-ff5ea222c2b28}} of expression medium containing {{ph:1774024680081-2608acdba053b}} with {{ph:1774024680081-b41278cd1047f8}} of overnight starter culture.
Grow the culture at 37 C with shaking until OD600 reaches {{ph:1774024680081-fab6fafbcf158}}.
Add IPTG to a final concentration of {{ph:1774024680081-587c106fae95a}} to induce protein expression.
Shift the culture to {{ph:1774024680081-2ce357c07b8e68}} and continue shaking for {{ph:1774024680081-1e13340d6a10c}}.
Harvest cells by centrifugation at {{ph:1774024680081-d82f101f8190e8}} for {{ph:1774024680081-ad983f4a2f5b68}} at {{ph:1774024680081-4962dce7ed7eb8}}.

data.name: Ni-NTA Purification of His-Tagged Protein
data.purpose: Purify a His-tagged recombinant protein using nickel affinity resin.

steps.text: Resuspend the cell pellet in 100 mL of lysis buffer
Lyse the cells using sonication and clarify the lysate by centrifugation at 10,000 rpm for 30 mins.
Equilibrate 5 mL of Ni-NTA resin with 20 mL of lysis buffer.
Load the clarified lysate onto the resin.
Wash the resin with 40 mL of wash buffer containing 20 mM imidazole.
Elute the bound protein using 6 mL of elution buffer containing 300 mM imidazole.
Collect fractions and analyze them by SDS-PAGE.

data.troubleshooting:
Problem: Target protein does not bind resin; Possible cause: His-tag is inaccessible or imidazole concentration in binding buffer is too high; Solution: Reduce imidazole in the binding step and confirm the His-tag is intact
Problem: High contaminant bands in elution; Possible cause: Wash conditions were too weak; Solution: Increase wash stringency by adjusting imidazole concentration or wash volume

protocol:1774024712936-cdad2f729e908.label: TEV Protease Cleavage of Fusion Protein

data.purpose: Remove an affinity or solubility tag from a fusion protein using TEV protease.

steps.text: Exchange the fusion protein into cleavage buffer using {{ph:1774024712936-7dba43a18d95f8}}.
Add TEV protease at an enzyme-to-substrate ratio of {{ph:1774024712936-8060b8a60ca3b}}.
Incubate the reaction at {{ph:1774024712936-51cd47e4df67a}} for {{ph:1774024712936-bf51d65dc5d7e}}.
Remove an aliquot before and after cleavage for SDS-PAGE analysis.
Separate the cleaved tag, uncleaved protein, and TEV protease using {{ph:1774024712936-e83fc6a9af4a2}}.

data.troubleshooting:
Problem: Incomplete cleavage; Possible cause: Insufficient TEV amount or inaccessible cleavage site; Solution: Increase incubation time, increase TEV ratio, or optimize buffer composition
Problem: Protein precipitates during cleavage; Possible cause: Protein is unstable in cleavage buffer; Solution: Test alternative salt concentration, glycerol level, or lower protein concentration

data.name: Avi-Tag Protein Biotinylation
data.purpose: Biotinylate an Avi-tagged protein for downstream binding assays or immobilization.

steps.text: Prepare the biotinylation reaction by combining {{ph:1774024745003-093192d094133}} of Avi-tagged protein, {{ph:1774024745003-fbbbfbaa73e5b}} of BirA, {{ph:1774024745003-d6f73ec6557a1}} of biotin, ATP, and buffer.
Remove excess free biotin using {{ph:1774024745003-d1b54c3887f0f8}}.
